title.en: My Song of the Deep: Psalm 104

region.en: Jerusalem (symbolic pin for the temple singers)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（聖殿歌手的象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE; collected in the Psalter (Ezra-Nehemiah era stabilization); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The great nature-poem of the Psalter: God wrapped in light 'as with a garment', riding the clouds as a chariot, laying the beams of His chambers on the waters, sending springs for wild asses, grass for cattle, wine 'to gladden the heart of man'. Sinners vanish; 'my song of praise shall be sweet to Him' — creation as ongoing, ordered joy.
summary.zh: 詩篇的自然頌歌：神以光為衣，乘雲如車，在 waters 上立殿宇之棟樑；使泉源流於野驢，草生於牲畜，酒「悅人心」。罪人消沒；「願我的吟頌蒙他喜悅」——創造是持續而有序的喜樂。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul; O LORD my God, Thou art very great; Thou art clothed with glory and majesty. Who coverest Thyself with light as with a garment, who stretchest the heavens like a curtain; who layest the beams of Thy chambers in the waters, who makest the clouds Thy chariot, who walkest upon the wings of the wind; who makest Thy angels into winds, and Thy ministers a flaming fire.

The Psalm walks through creation's economy: springs in the valleys 'that the wild asses of the dry places quench their thirst', birds nesting by them, wine 'that gladdeneth the heart of man', oil 'to make the face to shine', bread 'to strengthen the heart'; the sun rises, lions roar, man goes forth to his work until evening. The poet ends: 'I will sing unto the LORD as long as I live... my meditation of Him shall be sweet; I will be glad in the LORD.' Paraphrase of Psalm 104:10-34 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

region.en: Jerusalem (symbolic pin for the temple singers)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（聖殿歌手的象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE; collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Under the full sky the poet asks the question the eden narrative answers in story: 'When I behold Thy heavens... what is man, that Thou art mindful of him?' The answer: 'Thou hast made him but little lower than the divine, and hast crowned him with glory and honour... to have dominion over the works of Thy hands' — man the ruler of the deep creatures named in the first creation account.
summary.zh: 仰望穹蒼之際，詩人問出伊甸敘事所答之問：「我觀看你指頭所造的天……人算什麼，你竟顧念他？」答案是：「你叫他比天使微小一點，並賜他榮耀尊貴為冠冕……派他管理你手所造的」——人為首章受造深處之物的治理者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth! Whose majesty is recounted above the heavens... When I behold Thy heavens, the work of Thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which Thou hast established; what is man, that Thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that Thou thinkest of him? Yet Thou hast made him but little lower than the divine, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.

title.en: Thou Didst Break the Heads of the Sea-Monsters: Psalm 74
title.zh: 你曾打破水中大魚的頭：詩篇七十四篇

region.zh: 耶路撒冷，廢墟（被擄哀歌）

texts.period: Composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE (community lament); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: In a lament over the burned sanctuary the poet still recalls the old combat myth: 'O God, my King... Thou didst break the heads of the sea-monsters in the waters. Thou brakest the heads of Leviathan... Thou didst set springs and torrents' — creation as defeat of primordial waters, preserved in poetry long after Genesis had excluded the battle from prose.
summary.zh: 聖所被焚的哀歌中仍存古老爭戰神話：「神我的王……你曾打破水中大魚的頭。你曾砸碎利未亞坦的頭……你曾使泉源谿川湧流」——創造即戰勝原初大水，詩體長存，而創世記散文已除其爭戰。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Cross-tradition chaoskampf cluster (Tiamat parallels); tag noted as interpretive.

passages.text: O God, my King, from of old, who wroughtest deliverance in the midst of the earth; Thou didst break the sea by Thy strength; Thou didst break the heads of the sea-monsters in the waters. Thou didst break the heads of Leviathan in pieces, and gavest him to be food to the folk inhabiting the wilderness. Thou didst cleave fountain and brook; Thou driedst up ever-flowing rivers.

title.en: The LORD Said Unto My Lord: Psalm 2
title.zh: 耶和華對我主說：詩篇二篇

region.zh: 錫安，大衛之城（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 10th-6th c. BCE (royal psalm); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: A coronation psalm: the nations rage and 'the kings of the earth set themselves... against the LORD, and against His anointed'; from heaven the King laughs. 'I will tell of the decree: the LORD said unto me: Thou art My son... Ask of Me, and I will give the nations for Thine inheritance' — the king installed on Zion, ruling 'with a rod of iron', warned: 'Do homage to the son, lest he be angry.'
summary.zh: 加冕詩：外邦喧嚷，「地上的君王一起起來……敵擋耶和華並他的受膏者」；天上的王發笑。「我必傳聖旨：耶和華曾對我說：你是我的兒子……你求我，我就將列國賜你為基業」——受膏者坐於錫安聖山，以鐵杖轄管，警告：「當親吻其子，恐怕他發怒。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Royal psalms acquired messianic readings; record describes the royal-court setting.

passages.text: I will tell of the decree; the LORD said unto me: 'Thou art My son, this day have I begotten thee. Ask of Me, and I will give the nations for Thine inheritance, and the ends of the earth for Thy possession. Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; Thou shalt dash them to pieces like a potter's vessel.'

title.en: The LORD Is My Shepherd: Psalm 23
title.zh: 耶和華是我的牧者：詩篇二十三篇

region.en: Jerusalem (symbolic pin for the temple singers)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（聖殿歌手的象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The most-recited psalm in the world: green pastures, still waters, the valley of the shadow of death walked 'I fear no evil, for Thou art with me', the table in the presence of enemies, anointing, overflowing cup, and the ending — 'I shall dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.'
summary.zh: 世上最常誦讀的詩篇：青草地、安歇水、死蔭的幽谷「我必不遭害，因為你與我同在」，敵人面前的筵席、膏油、滿溢的杯，與結語——「我且要住在耶和華的殿中，直到永遠」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures; He leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul; He guideth me in straight paths for His name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff, they comfort me.

title.en: A Broken and Contrite Heart: Psalm 51
title.zh: 憂傷痛悔的心：詩篇五十一篇

texts.period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE (superscription links to David and Bathsheba); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The penitential psalm par excellence, headed 'when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba': 'Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin... Hide Thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities. Create me a clean heart, O God... restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation'. Sacrifice is redefined: 'the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, Thou wilt not despise.'
summary.zh: 悔罪詩之首，標題「先知拿單來見他之後，他與拔示巴犯了罪之後」：「求你將我的罪孽洗除淨盡，並潔除我的罪……求你掩面不看我的罪，塗抹我一切的罪孽。神啊，求你為我造清潔的心……求你使我仍得救恩之樂」。祭物重釋：「神所要的祭，就是憂傷的靈；憂傷痛悔的心，你必不輕看。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Recited daily in the morning liturgy.

passages.text: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to Thy lovingkindness; according unto the multitude of Thy compassions, blot out my transgressions. Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin; for I know my transgressions; and my sin is ever before me.

title.en: By the Rivers of Babylon: Psalm 137
title.zh: 巴比倫河畔：詩篇一三七篇

texts.period: Composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE (exilic); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The exile's psalm: 'By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion. We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that led us captive required of us songs... saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD'S song in a foreign land?' — ending with the darkest imprecation in the Psalter, against Edom and against Babylon's infants, kept as the memory of atrocity.
summary.zh: 被擄之詩：「我們曾在巴比倫的河邊坐下，一追想錫安就哭了。我們把琴掛在那裡的柳樹上。因為在那裡擄掠我們的要我們唱歌……說：給我們唱一篇錫安的歌吧。我們怎能在外邦唱耶和華的歌呢？」——末節咒詛以東與巴比倫的嬰孩，作暴行記憶之最暗遺存。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The closing verses preserve ancient war-curse conventions; record states the text.

passages.text: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion. We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that led us captive required of us songs, and them that tormented us required of us mirth, saying: 'Sing us one of the songs of Zion.' How shall we sing the LORD'S song in a foreign land?

title.en: Teach Us to Number Our Days: Psalm 90
title.zh: 求你教我們數算自己的日子：詩篇九十篇

texts.period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE (attributed to Moses); collected in the Psalter; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The psalm of mortality, titled 'A Prayer of Moses': a thousand years as yesterday; a flood sweeping men asleep; seventy, or eighty by strength, years 'in which we travail'; the request that crowns the prayer — 'Teach us to number our days, that we may get us a heart of wisdom' — and the return: 'satisfy us in the morning with Thy lovingkindness... make us glad according to the days'.
summary.zh: 論必死之詩，題「神人摩西的祈禱」：千年如昨日；如洪水掃人入睡；七十歲，若強壯可到八十，「其中所矜誇的，不過是勞苦愁煩」。禱告的冠冕是：「求你指教我們怎樣數算自己的日子，好叫我們得著智慧的心」——及其回應：「求你使我們早早飽得你的慈愛……照著你使我們受苦的日子，和我們遭難的年歲，叫我們喜樂。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Lord, Thou hast been our dwelling-place in all generations. Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever Thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, Thou art God. ... The days of our years are three-score years and ten, or even by reason of strength fourscore years; yet is their pride but travail and vanity; for it is speedily gone, and we fly away. ... So teach us to number our days, that we may get us a heart of wisdom.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalm 90:1, 10, 12 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: Praise Ye the LORD: The Great Hallel
title.zh: 你們要讚美耶和華：大哈利路

texts.period: Composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE (Egyptian Hallel collected); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The Hallel — Psalms 113-118 — sung at the Passover Seder and the great festivals: God 'who dwelleth on high... that He may look down low upon heaven and upon the earth', raising the poor from the dust; Israel passing through the sea; 'the stone which the builders refused is become the head-stone'; and the thanksgiving refrain, 'His mercy endureth for ever'.
summary.zh: 哈利路——詩篇一一三至一一八——於逾越節家宴與大節期所唱：神「坐在至高之處，自己謙卑，觀看天上地下的事」，使貧窮人從灰塵裡抬舉；以色列過海；「匠人所棄的石頭，已成了房角的頭塊石頭」；並感謝的副歌：「他的慈愛永遠長存。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Hallel is living liturgy (Pesach, Sukkot, Shavuot, Rosh Chodesh).

passages.text: Praise ye the LORD! Praise, O ye servants of the LORD, praise the name of the LORD; blessed be the name of the LORD from this time forth and for ever. From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof the LORD'S name is to be praised. The LORD is high above all nations, and His glory above the heavens. ... The stone which the builders refused is become the head-stone of the corner. This is the LORD'S doing; it is marvellous in our eyes.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Psalms 113:1-4; 118:22-23 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: Wisdom Cries Aloud in the Streets: Proverbs 8
title.zh: 智慧在街市上呼喊：箴言八章

texts.period: Composed c. 8th-5th c. BCE (Solomonic collections); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Wisdom personified as a woman at the crossways, crying to the simple. Most remarkably, she claims a place at creation: 'The LORD made me at the beginning of His way, before His works of old... When He made a decree for the rain... then I was by Him, as a master-workman; and I was daily all delight, rejoicing always before Him.' Wisdom's antediluvian presence makes her a quasi-divine builder of the world.
summary.zh: 智慧被擬人化為道路口呼喊的女子，向愚蒙人發聲。最顯著處，她自述參與創造：「耶和華在祂道路的起頭，在太古創造我……祂為雨水設定例……那時我在祂那裡為工師，日日為祂所喜愛，常常在祂面前踴躍。」智慧先於世界而在，近乎為世界的營造者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Personified Wisdom later shaped Sophia traditions; tag interpretive.

passages.text: Doth not wisdom cry, and understanding put forth her voice? On the top of high places by the way, where the paths meet, she standeth; beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors, she crieth aloud. Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of men.

'When there were no depths, I was brought forth... Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, was I brought forth... When He gave to the sea His decree, that the waters should not transgress His commandment, when He appointed the foundations of the earth; then I was by Him, as a master-workman; and I was daily all delight, rejoicing always before Him; rejoicing in His habitable earth; and my delights are with the sons of men.' Paraphrase of Proverbs 8:24-31 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Vanity of Vanities: Koheleth under the Sun
title.zh: 虛空的虛空：日光之下的傳道者

region.en: Jerusalem (speaker styled 'son of David, king in Jerusalem')
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（講者自稱「在耶路撒冷作王的大衛的兒子」）

texts.period: Composed c. 3rd c. BCE (Persian-Hellenistic era); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The sceptical sage's sermon: 'Vanity of vanities... all is vanity'; a time to be born and a time to die; the race not to the swift; 'the dead know not any thing'; the final frame — 'fear God, and keep His commandments; for this is the whole duty of man' — while the wheel turns: 'the sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he ariseth.'
summary.zh: 懷疑派智者的講道：「虛空的虛空……凡事都是虛空」；生有時死有時；快跑的未必能贏；「死了的人毫無所知」；末段的框架：「敬畏神，謹守他的誡命，這是人所當盡的本分」——而輪迴不止：「日頭出來，日頭落下，急歸所出之地。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read at Sukkot in the Five Scrolls cycle.

passages.text: Vanity of vanities, saith Koheleth; vanity of vanities, all is vanity. What profit hath man of all his labour wherein he laboureth under the sun? One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh; and the earth abideth for ever. The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he ariseth.

title.en: I Am Black but Comely: The Song of Songs

region.en: Vineyards of Judah and royal palaces (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 猶大葡萄園與王宮（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 5th-3rd c. BCE (lyric collection); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The most openly amorous book in scripture, canonized as the love between God and Israel: 'I am black, but comely... Look not upon me, because I am swarthy'; 'Behold, thou art fair, my love'; the garden locked, 'a fountain sealed'; and the ending, 'Set me as a seal upon thy heart... for love is strong as death.' 'Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it.'
summary.zh: 聖經中最直白的情歌，正典化為神與以色列之愛：「我雖黑卻秀美……不要因日頭把我曬黑了就輕看我」；「我的佳偶，你甚美麗」；關鎖的園、「禁閉的井」；結尾：「求你將我印在你心上……因為愛情如死之堅強。」「眾水不能熄滅愛情，洪水也不能淹沒。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Rabbi Akiva: 'the whole world is not worth the day on which the Song of Songs was given'; allegorical reading is the normative Jewish one.

passages.text: The song of songs, which is Solomon's. Oh that he would kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; for thy love is better than wine. I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem... Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon?
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Song of Songs 1:1-7 (public domain), condensed.

passages.text: 'A garden shut is my sister, my bride; a rock-mystic spring, a fountain sealed' — the bride's body is temple-garden language. The book ends with the invitation of love's strength: 'Set me as a seal upon thy heart, as a seal upon thine arm; for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave... Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it.' Paraphrase of Song of Songs 4:12; 8:6-7 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Song of Songs 4:12; 8:6-7 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: How Doth the City Sit Solitary: Lamentations

region.zh: 耶路撒冷，公元前586年後的廢墟

texts.period: Composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE (response to the destruction); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The five laments of the destroyed city, chanted in acrostic on Tisha B'Av: 'How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people!' — Judah gone into exile, 'none to comfort her'; children faint for hunger; but chapter 3's centrepiece of hope: 'His compassions fail not. They are new every morning; great is Thy faithfulness. The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in Him.'
summary.zh: 毀城五首哀歌，按字母離合體於聖殿被毀日吟誦：「先前滿有人民的城，現在何竟孤獨！」——猶大被擄，「無人安慰」；孩童因饑餓昏倒；但三章的核心盼望：「他的憐憫不斷絕，每早晨都是新的；你的信實極其廣大。我心裡說：耶和華是我的分；因此，我要仰望他。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read on Tisha B'Av to recall the destruction of the Temples.

passages.text: How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people! How is she become as a widow! She that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become tributary! ... For these things I weep; mine eye, mine eye runneth down with water; because the comforter that should refresh my soul is far from me; my children are desolate, because the enemy prevailed.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Lamentations 1:1; 1:16 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

passages.text: Chapter 3 turns the dirge into hope: 'It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed... They are new every morning; great is Thy faithfulness. The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in Him. The LORD is good unto them that wait for Him... It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.' Paraphrase of Lamentations 3:22-26 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
